audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers read Lucian, Lucian, Lucian, Lucian, Skill, Skill, Lucian against a packet chart of Skill, Lucian, Lucian, Skill, Mel, Mel, Mel — and against this page's own whys[4..6], which all say Mel takes over from 6 onward.
audit.why: Radiant Volley is 950 range to Lucian's 500, so level 1 is not his; and from 6 Golden Eclipse plus her range genuinely flip the lane, which is what the prose already says.
audit.corrected: Rows 0 and 3 set to Skill and rows 4, 5, 6 to Mel in both layers as matched pairs, ratings re-scaled to 5/5/3/3/2. NOTE for the mirror: the mel__lucian audit recorded these side flips as 'NOT FIXABLE BY PROPOSAL' because it believed apply-proposals.js refuses full-layer edits with a short `before`. Per the run instructions that belief is false — ENUM_FIELD exempts phases[N].side and the sub-25-character skip applies, so these land cleanly. The mirror's chart should be re-run rather than left manual.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[4] described level 6 as Lucian's spike; on this lane 6 is Mel's, and no cooldown appeared anywhere.
audit.why: Golden Eclipse is 120/100/80s with effectively global range and detonates every Overwhelm stack she has put on you, so her 6 outclasses his. Rebuttal is 38/35/33/29/26s — a very long cooldown, which makes 'wait it out' a real plan rather than a platitude.
audit.corrected: phases[4].why now names Golden Eclipse and what it does; Rebuttal's 38s written into report[5].t, dosFull[2].d and 'mid'.
sources: enemyKit Mel R cd 120/100/80 and P Overwhelm text

audit.whatIsWrong: THE BIG ONE: the content layer says five separate times that Mel's R reflects. It does not. Her W, Rebuttal, is the reflect. Golden Eclipse (R) is a global Overwhelm detonation with no reflect component at all.
audit.why: Riot's W text: 'Mel forms a barrier around herself that reflects enemy projectiles back at the attacker, prevents her from taking damage'. Riot's R text: 'Mel strikes all enemies marked with Overwhelm regardless of their distance from her'. The page therefore teaches a Lucian to hold The Culling for her ultimate — the wrong cooldown entirely. A player following it will happily channel into an active Rebuttal (because her R is up, so she 'can't reflect yet') and reflect his own ultimate into his face, while still eating the real R from across the map.
audit.corrected: Every reflect reference re-pointed to Rebuttal (W) in whys[4], spikes[2].text, mid, late and wants.foe[1], with the 38s cooldown given so the bait-and-wait advice is actionable. Golden Eclipse described correctly as the global Overwhelm execute.
sources: enemyKit Mel W and R text

edits.before: Your edge is already thinning here. You stay slightly favored at 4-5 on the strength of your earlier spikes, but your mana strains and her Q poke starts to add up faster than you can close the distance. At 6 the lane flips: do NOT reflexively fire The Culling at her — her R reflects projectiles and damage, so a careless channel feeds your own burst back into your low HP pool. Bait the reflect with an E-dash and a single Lightslinger shot, wait it out, then commit. If you didn't get a lead by now, you're playing from behind.

edits.before: This is her game now. Once her first AP item is online her Q chunks you out of every wave and you have no way to all-in past her R reflect and W zone, while you're a weak scaler who falls off hard for an ADC top. Your only path is a lead you built at Levels 2-6 — if you have it, sidelane and pressure before she's full. If you don't, accept you can't 1v1 her, group with your team, and use The Culling as pickoff burst on targets who can't reflect it, never as a duel button into Mel herself.

notes: Deliberately NOT restated from the mirror: mel__lucian's headline finding is that Solar Snare's root switches on Lightslinger's bonus damage. Riot's Lightslinger clause is 'when a nearby ENEMY Champion is immobilized' — from Lucian's seat the enemy is Mel, so the trigger reads as Mel being immobilized, not Lucian being rooted by Solar Snare. The mirror's phrasing ('immobilising him switches on Lightslinger's bonus damage') points the other way. One of the two readings is wrong and the kit text does not settle which, so I wrote nothing about it on this side rather than ship a contradiction that mirror-fix.js would then propagate. Question logged. Second note: the mirror also recorded its own chart rows as unfixable by proposal on a false premise about the applier's minimum `before` length — worth re-running mel__lucian's chart.
